headline: The belly rallies again as Treasuries slip and stocks slide: the 5Y MGS falls 4.7bp to 3.551% and the 3s5s10s fly hits a one-year low
summary: Malaysian government bonds gained across the curve on Friday, led again by the belly: on FAST's curve the 3Y fell 2.9bp to 3.372%, the 5Y 4.7bp to 3.551% (−9.8bp on the week) and the 10Y 1.8bp to 3.823%, so the 3s5s10s fly dropped to −9.3bp, the 2nd percentile of the past year. GII lagged, leaving the 10Y GII at 3.863%, 4.0bp over MGS, and the 5Y GII 4.7bp over, the widest gap of the year. Hong Leong Bank's IRS closes as of Nov 19 were flat to 1bp higher (5Y 3.60%, 10Y 3.77%), which put the 5Y swap spread at +0.2bp and the 10Y at −7.1bp, both still in the bottom 5% of the past year. FX-swap implied ringgit yields (Nov 20, indicative) were 2.90% at 3 months and 3.02% at 1 year, 5.4bp and 3.2bp under onshore rates, about 0.5bp further under than on Thursday. Financial and SOE trading was thin (three trades by this run), with government-guaranteed DanaInfra paper at 38–39bp over MGS, and FAST's corporate curves still carry Nov 19 levels.
drivers: Belly squeeze after the 3Y reopening, with no auction next week

The RM5bn reopening of the 3Y MGS 3/29 on Thursday went well enough for Hong Leong Bank to call it decent, and its tender calendar shows no government auction next week, so dealers bought duration into a supply break. On Thursday govvies volume eased 8% to RM6.34bn and the GII share fell to 27%, with the 5Y MGS 6/31 down 3bp; on Friday the 5Y fell another 4.7bp and the 7Y 3.2bp against 1.8bp at 10Y and 0.1bp at 30Y. The 3s5s10s fly is now −9.3bp, 4.7bp lower on the day and near its one-year low of −10.2bp (average −1.2bp), so the belly is rich to the wings.
Treasuries and the equity rout outweighed record exports

October exports rose 61.1% y/y to a record RM239.2bn against a 48.7% consensus (September 54.5%), led by E&E shipments up 87.2%, a growth beat that supports the Q1 2027 hike calls from HSBC, ANZ and Kenanga; bonds ignored it. The KLCI fell 0.61% to 1,556.51, a 15-month low, on data-centre and tech selling, and international reserves eased to US$132.1bn at Nov 13 from US$132.6bn. The risk-off tone and a weaker US session (below) did more for MGS than the data did.
US yields lower; ringgit and FX swap barely move

The US 10Y closed 3bp lower at 5.04% on Thursday after jobless claims of 203k (f 197k) and a Philadelphia Fed index of 6.3 (f 20.1), and traded near 4.99% in Asia on Friday as stocks fell. At the one-year daily beta of 0.15 that implies only −0.5bp for the 10Y MGS, which fell 1.8bp, so most of the day's rally was local. USD/MYR was flat at 4.1105 at 6pm (BNM reference 4.1125, +0.05%; +0.69% on the week). The FX-swap implied curve moved by 0.1bp on the day and the gap to onshore by about 0.5bp, too small to read on indicative quotes; FXEmpire's forward points have not changed since Nov 18, so the implied moves are mostly the US bill yields.
IRS steady while MGS rally: swap spreads off the lows

On Hong Leong Bank's Nov 19 snapshot the IRS curve closed 3.64% (1Y), 3.58% (3Y), 3.60% (5Y), 3.67% (7Y) and 3.77% (10Y), flat to +1bp on the day but 5–7bp lower on the week and 12–18bp lower on the month; 1s5s is −4bp and 5s10s +17bp. With MGS rallying underneath, the 5Y swap spread rose 2.2bp to +0.2bp (3rd percentile, one-year average +10.2bp) and the 10Y 1.1bp to −7.1bp (4th percentile, average +8.0bp). These are one bank's indicative closes and 1–2bp daily moves are within its noise; if the IRS holds on Monday's snapshot, Friday's 4.7bp MGS rally would widen the 5Y spread further.
data: Record exports on E&E; firms the growth case for a Q1 2027 hike, but MGS rallied anyway.
Small dip; still ample cover for ringgit smoothing.
RM5bn; HLB calls it decent (cover ratio not found in sources)
Cleared without a cheapening; next week has no government tender.
Slightly soft; keeps a Q1 2027 hike likely but not urgent.
A beat led by investment and E&E exports; firmed Q1 2027 hike calls.
MGS +RM4.7bn to a record RM238.2bn (33.1%); GII −RM1.3bn
Foreign demand for MGS remains the anchor for the belly and the 10Y.
Held with a firmer tone; next meeting Jan 21, 2027.
view: Take profit on the belly and fade its richness: the 5Y overweight from 3.636% (Nov 17) closes at 3.551% for +8.5bp, 0.1bp short of the 3.55% target, because the 3s5s10s fly at −9.3bp (2nd percentile, average −1.2bp) now prices the supply break in full; the new trade sells the 5Y against the 3Y and 10Y (pay the fly) at −9.3bp, target −3bp, stop −13bp. I expect the 10Y to hold 3.76–3.88% over the next two weeks and would buy it only at 3.88%. The pay-5Y-IRS-vs-long-5Y-MGS swap-spread trade from −4.6bp is 4.8bp in the money at +0.2bp (as of Nov 19); keep the +3bp target and raise the stop to −4bp, and stay out of the 10Y version while it sits at −7.1bp (−16.0bp in a month) with receivers still active. The FX swap prices ringgit under onshore rates beyond one month (3M implied 2.90%, gap −5.4bp; 1Y 3.02%, gap −3.2bp; 1M 2.95%, +1.9bp) and only about 15bp over the OPR at 3 months, which fits steady demand to hold ringgit rather than dollar stress; with the 3Y still 62.2bp over the OPR (77th percentile, average 48.3bp), the front end is cheap to the swap market, and I lower the 3Y buy level to 3.42%. GII lagged the rally: the 10Y GII is 4.0bp over MGS (92nd percentile), 0.2bp offside on the prefer-GII call from 3.8bp (target 1.5bp, stop 6.5bp), and the 5Y GII gap of 4.7bp is the widest of the year. In credit, SOE trades averaged 50.0bp over MGS over five sessions against 73.9bp for financial issuers, with government-guaranteed DanaInfra at 38.0bp the cleaner value; the AAA and Cagamas 5Y spreads on the page (55.6bp and 44.1bp) compare stale Nov 19 corporate curves with today's lower MGS, and like-for-like they were 50.9bp and 39.4bp, so I hold and do not add. Treasuries explain little: over four weeks the 10Y MGS is down 5.7bp while the US 10Y rose 8bp, a +2.6bp Treasury-linked part and −8.3bp local; the daily flow signal is −0.50, on the sell-off line with the regime neutral, and its sell-off calls were right only 38.5% of the time since mid-2022 in an in-sample back-test (Sharpe 1.07 outright, 1.33 hedged, but 0.27 hedged since September 2024), so I do not lean on it.

buckets.name: Front end 3Y vs OPR
buckets.why: The 3Y MGS is 3.372% (−2.9bp, −4.6bp on the week), 62.2bp over the 2.75% OPR, the 77th percentile of the past year (average 48.3bp). FX-swap implied yields of 2.95% at 1 month and 2.90% at 3 months sit only 15–20bp over the OPR, +1.9bp and −5.4bp against onshore rates (the 3M gap 0.5bp wider under on the day), so the swap market is not paying for an early hike. Nov 19 call (buy at 3.45%): not triggered; the 3Y kept rallying after its reopening.
buckets.call: Buy the 3Y MGS 3/29 at 3.42% (lowered from 3.45%); target 3.33%, stop 3.50%.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (3s5s10s fly)
buckets.stance: Took profit; now pay the fly
buckets.why: The 5Y fell 4.7bp to 3.551% (−9.8bp on the week; 75th percentile, average 3.446%) and the fly is −9.3bp, the 2nd percentile (average −1.2bp, low −10.2bp). The Nov 17 overweight from 3.636% reached 3.551%, 0.1bp short of target: closed for +8.5bp. The 5Y swap spread was +0.2bp on Nov 19 (+2.2bp on the day, 3rd percentile, average +10.2bp).
buckets.call: Pay the fly (sell 5Y vs 3Y and 10Y, duration-weighted) at −9.3bp; target −3bp, stop −13bp. Swap-spread trade (pay 5Y IRS vs long 5Y MGS) from −4.6bp: open at +0.2bp, target +3bp, stop raised to −4bp.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y is 3.823% (−1.8bp, −3.9bp on the week), the 77th percentile of the past year (average 3.671%, range 3.440–4.184%). It yields 121.7bp less than the US 10Y, 22.3bp below its 130-day average gap and in the bottom 6% of the year; the 10Y swap spread is −7.1bp (Nov 19, 4th percentile, average +8.0bp). Nov 19 buy level (3.90%) not reached.
buckets.call: Buy at 3.88%, target 3.80%, stop 3.95%; no position in the middle of the range.

buckets.name: Long end 10s30s
buckets.why: 10s30s is 51.4bp (+1.7bp, +4.4bp on the week), the 86th percentile (average 46.9bp), as the 30Y held at 4.337% (−0.1bp) while the 20Y fell 2.1bp. The GII 7/40 cleared at 4.158% with a 2.32x cover on Nov 12, and with no tender next week the long end has no supply test. Nov 19 neutral call unchanged.
buckets.call: Neutral; switch to flatteners after a long auction draws a cover above 2.5x.

buckets.name: GII vs MGS 10Y
buckets.why: The 10Y GII at 3.863% (−1.0bp) is 4.0bp over MGS (+0.8bp), the 92nd percentile of the past year (average 1.0bp); the 5Y GII gap is 4.7bp, the widest of the year (average −1.3bp), as GII lagged the belly rally and its share of trading fell to 27% on Thursday (HLB). Nov 18 call from 3.8bp: 0.2bp offside.
buckets.call: Prefer 10Y GII over MGS; target 1.5bp, stop 6.5bp. Same preference at 5Y.

buckets.name: AAA credit 5Y
buckets.why: FAST's AAA 5Y (4.107%, still dated Nov 19) shows 55.6bp over today's 5Y MGS, a one-year high (average 28.1bp), but like-for-like on Nov 19 it was 50.9bp: most of the widening is the MGS rally against a curve that has not updated. Nov 18 first slice at about 49bp: 1.9bp offside like-for-like. UOB Malaysia's AAA ratings were affirmed (HLB).
buckets.call: Add the rest at 55bp on a same-day print; target 40bp, stop 62bp.

buckets.name: Cagamas 5Y vs MGS
buckets.why: Cagamas 5Y at 3.992% (Nov 19) shows 44.1bp over today's MGS on the page (one-year high, average 22.6bp) and 39.4bp like-for-like; Khazanah 5Y was 32.3bp over on Nov 19. Over five sessions financial issuers traded 73.9bp over MGS (23 trades) and SOEs 50.0bp (38 trades; DanaInfra 38.0bp across 14, Prasarana 41.6bp, LPPSA 39.7bp). Nov 18 entry at about 38bp: 1.4bp offside like-for-like.

watch: Next: Fed Governor Waller's speech (Nov 20 US), a week with no MGS/GII tender (HLB calendar), US Thanksgiving (Nov 26), the Fed's Dec 8–9 meeting where Waller argues for 50bp, and BNM's next MPC on Jan 21, 2027.
